note: Root-family split of a certified corpus; nothing was synthesized. v2 supersedes openui_verified_train_v1, which was untrainable: admission checked fewer contracts than the trainer, so records the trainer refuses reached the bucket and every screening arm exited non-zero. v1 is immutable and stays as built. Each recommendation names an admission-time action the build performs, verified by re-measuring the admitted records rather than asserting it. Receipts bind to the split-policy plan hash and the dataset manifest hash. No gate, threshold or output contract was weakened; admission applies more of them. These receipts clear SFT for openui_verified_train_v2 only; the upstream fixes to openui_verified_v1 remain open against that corpus's own feedback artifact.

actions.note: Found by running the loop, not by reading the corpus. TwoTowerModel.from_records asserts four record contracts before it builds anything -- assert_no_template_semantic_labels, assert_canonical_template_markers, assert_symbol_only_output and assert_role_safe_output -- and raises on the first violation, which takes the whole training arm down. Admission applied a narrower set, so records carrying a placeholder in a non-content property (for example ':slot_0' in RadialChart.labels) or a semantic role label in the prompt reached the train bucket and made it untrainable. Admission now applies all four at a new role_safety stage, using the record's own target_kind and falling back to the document kind the model resolves for a record that declares none. Every refusal is recorded in rejected.jsonl: 256 across the three splits. Re-measured after the rebuild: 0 of 893 admitted records fail any of the four. The contracts were applied more widely at admission, never relaxed. Re-certifying openui_verified_v1 so its records satisfy the trainer's contracts stays open against that corpus.

before.symptom: every screening arm exited non-zero at TwoTowerModel.from_records

actions.note: Audited quality_report.json and rejected.jsonl: the split build rejects every record that fails the current symbol-only output contract at admission and never patches one, which is exactly the action the recommendation prescribes. The 90 OutputContractError rejections are visible in rejected.jsonl and the admitted bucket contains none. Re-certifying the parent corpus openui_verified_v1 under symbol_only/v2 stays open against that corpus's own feedback artifact.

The admitted bucket holds 893 records under 893 distinct ids, so no consumer can re-identify a record. Namespacing the parent corpus stays open against that corpus.
